reason: The text clearly portrays the Hebrews (Israel) as followers of Yahweh (יְהוָה) through multiple narrative elements: (1) Moses acts as Yahweh's intermediary, communicating God's directives to the people; (2) the military victory depends entirely on God's power—Israel prevails when Moses raises his hand with the rod of God (מַטֵּה הָאֱלֹהִים) and falters when he lowers it, demonstrating divine agency; (3) Moses builds an altar to Yahweh (יְהוָה נִסִּי—'the LORD is my banner') in commemoration; (4) Yahweh directly commands Moses and promises ongoing warfare against Amalek on Israel's behalf; (5) the closing statement (יָד עַל־ כֵּס יָהּ מִלְחָמָה לַיהוָה) emphasizes that Yahweh actively fights for Israel. The entire account depicts Israel under divine guidance and protection, wholly dependent on Yahweh's power for their survival and success.
